title: The Sixty-Second Light
status: concept-proposal (Creative Director, 2026-11-19; not approved; awaiting owner review)
hook_line: Our hallway light lasts sixty seconds. There are rules.
first_visual: A glowing push-button timer switch in a dark corridor; a laminated card beside it, rule 4 underlined twice.

beats.visual: Ivy's finger hovers at the glowing timer switch; a laminated card beside it.
beats.vo: Our hallway light lasts sixty seconds. There are rules.

beats.visual: She presses once; the corridor lights warm.
She walks, not running, past doors.
The light cuts out at 41 s; dark; she stands still.
beats.vo: Three: if it goes out early, stand still and say your number.

beats.visual: Ivy, in darkness, whispers 'Nine.' From behind door 9, her own voice: 'Nine.'
Card close-up: 4. If something answers with your number, don't argue.
Light returns; Ivy's key won't turn in door 9.
beats.vo: I didn't argue. So it kept it.

beats.visual: She opens the numberless door at the end: residents sitting silently in the dark, each holding a pen.
beats.vo: Everyone who didn't argue lives here.

beats.visual: Card close-up: new handwriting writes itself: 5. Argue. Moth on the switch plate.

ending: On the card, new handwriting appears: '5. Argue.'
loop_note: No. It ends on the new rule.

originality_review: Original 'rules' structure. The rules are a building notice, not a family member's behaviour, so it does not use the 'If your mom ever...' template. The twist (the rules are authored by those who lost) is ours.
scores_basis: Initial editorial judgement, 2026-11-19. topic_demand is an estimate linked to research/WEEKLY_TREND_REPORT.md categories, not a measurement of this concept.
concept: The Vesper Court hallway light has a 60-second timer and a rules card. Ivy follows the rules exactly and loses her flat to whatever answers with her number. The rules were written by everyone who obeyed them, and she adds the rule they were missing.

hooks.line: Our hallway light lasts sixty seconds. There are rules.
hooks.first_visual: A glowing push-button timer switch in a dark corridor; a laminated card beside it, rule 4 underlined twice.

hooks.line: The light went out at forty-one seconds.
hooks.first_visual: A corridor plunging into darkness mid-step.

hooks.line: I said my flat number. Something said it back.
hooks.first_visual: A dark door; a voice answers from inside.

hooks.line: Rule four: if something answers with your number, don't argue.
hooks.first_visual: Close on a laminated rule, a fingertip under it.

hooks.line: There's a door at the end with no number.
hooks.first_visual: A plain door where the light never reaches.

setting: Vesper Court third-floor hallway; timer switch, doors 7-12, a numberless door at the end.
conflict: Ivy must reach her door before the timer ends, by the rules.
escalation: The light cuts early; she says 'Nine'; her own voice answers from inside flat 9.
reveal: Behind the numberless door sit all the residents who didn't argue, waiting in the dark, each holding a pen.
